newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares battle against Dow slide at start.
newsitem.headline: German shares battle against Dow slide at start.

text.p: German shares on Friday recorded only slight losses at the start of bourse trade following the sharp fall recorded overnight on Wall Street as fears of a rise in U.S. interest rates resurfaced.
With the dollar back up above 1.700 marks, however, traders were fairly confident that the German share losses would be limited, at least until publication of key U.S. economic data later on today.

"I don't see any sell-off at the moment. But after the U.S. figures, I'm not predicting anything," said one dealer. U.S. producer prices and industrial production data for February are expected later.
The DAX-30 index of top German shares fell 17.19 points, 0.51 percent, to 3,332.62 in early trade. March DAX futures were 33.0 points lower at 3,336.0.
Traders noted that the recent volatility of the market meant that forecasting the extent of price movements and identifying support levels was becoming more difficult.
One said, however, that the volumes that accompanied falls on Thursday had been relatively high, a possible indication of future selling pressure.

Software group SAP was one of the few shares to buck the downward trend, with its preference shares up 5.40 to 279.90 on IBIS. SAP said on Thursday it saw no reason to depart from earlier forecasts of strong first-quarter profit growth.
Deutsche Telekom continued its climb of recent days, moving to a new all-time high of 37.50 in electronic trade before easing back to 37.13, 21 pfennigs up on the day.

A Deutsche Telekom plan to start a traffic navigation and information service in joint venture with Daimler-Benz's Debis was viewed positively, with Daimler moving up 85 pfennigs to 127.30 in early bourse trade.
Engineering group Mannesmann was 30 marks lower at 622 on what dealers said was a continued reaction to a downgrade issued by Deutsche Bank earlier this week.
